blocks.text: In June a client launched to 181,619 impressions and 137 hours of video watch time. In August another filled his waitlist inside 24 hours. Both ran the same playbook, and most of it happened in the five days before either post went up.
Almost everyone treats the post as the launch, when it's about a fifth of the work and the fifth that happens last.

The part that decides the outcome is unglamorous. You build a list of fifty people who'd be genuinely pleased for you, message each of them personally four days out, and follow every message with a calendar invite for launch hour. The ask is the same three words every time: like, comment, save. Most people skip save, and it's the strongest of the three.

The mechanic that surprised me came from the August launch, which asked for two actions instead of one: comment below, and fill in the form. 554 people clicked the link and 343 commented. Those are two separate funnels, and most of the qualified signups never touched the link at all, so a post carrying only the link gets the 554 and nothing underneath.

Every section has a number against it, including the parts that went badly. Three weeks after his launch the same founder posted something motivational; it did 72,031 impressions, nearly double the launch, and produced seven followers and no signups.
